speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance and distribution of the blisters on your forearm? Do they appear clustered, and are they surrounded by redness?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your recent start on captopril and the presence of blisters on your forearm along with painful oral and genital ulcers, I need to determine if this is a drug reaction or another autoimmune condition. Are the blisters on your forearm itchy, and do you have any fever or swollen lymph nodes?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate, Anti-RNA_Polymerase_III_Antibodies.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Subacute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus (likely from captopril) or Stevens-Johnson Syndrome/TEN; pending lab results to confirm ANA or drug-specific antibodies.
